source.title: Design Equations for Broadside and Edgewise Stripline Couplers
source.publisher: Rogers Corporation, Advanced Circuit Materials Division, design note 3.2.1
source.transcribed: 2026-10-05, task D7-05, from page 2 of the note (the D7 impedance research copy rogers_bcs.pdf): the two 'Example designs' tables, values exactly as printed

conventions.assumptions: the note's: conductor thickness negligible (t = 0), equal widths, equal distance to both ground planes, dielectric fills the space between the planes, one relative permittivity for every layer
conventions.broadside: three boards: outer / center / outer; b = 2 * outer_board_in + center_board_in (the note: 'the sum of the thicknesses of the three boards'); strip spacing s = center_board_in; strip width = line_width_in
conventions.edge: two boards with one signal layer between them; b = 2 * board_in (ground plane spacing); s = spacing_in; w = width_in
conventions.printed_constants: the note writes Z0even = 188.3 / sqrt(er) * K(k')/K(k) and Z0odd = 296.1 * s / (sqrt(er) * atanh(k)) for broadside, and 30 * pi / sqrt(er) for the edgewise K-ratio prefactor (eta0/2, eta0*pi/4 and eta0/4 rounded)

er._source: not printed in the note: the Rogers data-sheet Dk of each laminate (RT/duroid 5880 2.20, 5870 2.33, 6002 2.94, 6006 6.15, 6010 10.2; TMM 3 3.27, TMM 4 4.50, TMM 6 6.00, TMM 10 9.20). The 5880/5870 rows share their geometry, and their printed Z0 ratio (9.83 / 9.55, 68.53 / 66.59) equals sqrt(2.33 / 2.20)
